words.title: Picture mode
words.detail: By default Jarvis reads only the words on your screen. Picture mode also lets a small picture reader look at the picture itself, so it can tell what a chart, a button or a photo shows. It runs on your PC's main chip (the CPU), not your graphics card, so your chat model is not slowed down - but it is SLOW, and how slow depends on your PC. Anything that looks like a key, a card number or a password is blacked out first, and if that part is missing no picture is used. Nothing leaves this PC and nothing is saved. If you have also turned on Pictures on an extra graphics card and it is running, a look uses that card's picture model instead, which is much faster, and this slow reader is only the backup. Off by default. Turning it on asks first, because a model has to be downloaded.
words.off_line: Picture mode is off. Jarvis reads the words on your screen only.
words.waiting_line: Waiting for your yes on the card. Nothing has changed yet.
words.missing: This PC's Jarvis is missing this feature. In PowerShell on the PC, in the Jarvis folder, run: .\scripts\apply-patches.ps1 . Then restart Jarvis.
words.steps_title: To set it up, paste this one line into PowerShell on your PC:
words.steps_note: It downloads the picture model from Ollama (ollama.com). We have not checked how big the download is, so expect a wait. Then it times one look on your PC and saves the number. Jarvis never downloads the model by itself.

why_words.unknown_install: Jarvis could not tell whether the picture model is installed (is Ollama running?).

why_words.start_failed: The picture reader could not start.
why_words.no_cleaner: The part of Jarvis that blacks out secrets in a picture is not installed, so no picture was used. Run .\scripts\apply-patches.ps1 in the Jarvis folder, then restart Jarvis.
why_words.clean_failed: Blacking out secrets in the picture did not work, so no picture was used.
why_words.slow: The picture reader took longer than {n} seconds.
why_words.error: The picture reader ran into an error.
why_words.empty: The picture reader had nothing to say about it.
why_words.on_graphics_card: The picture reader ended up on the graphics card, which is not what you switched on, so Jarvis stopped it.
why_words.changed: The picture model changed since you last timed it, so Jarvis will not use it. Run the set-up line in Settings again to time it.
why_words.cloud: The picture model's name looks like a cloud model, which would send your screen off this PC, so nothing was sent. Pick a model that runs on this PC.
why_words.superseded: You asked something newer, so this picture was skipped.
why_words.cancelled: The look was thrown away before the picture was read.
